clue.text: Support almost everything constitutional

parts.note: a leg is a support, as on a table

indicators.note: almost says the word for everything loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A claim that backing nearly everything is in line with the constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constitutional is permitted under the law of the state, so it is lawful.

clue.text: A note about 22 for 24

definitions.note: the answer to 24 down, a verb meaning to love deeply

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other here

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the answer to 22 across, meaning always

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing clue: a musical note wrapped round one answer stands for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to other answers in the grid: 22 across supplies the inner piece and 24 down is the definition, with 'about' wrapping the note around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep awe and worship, close in sense to adoring them.

clue.text: What's art anyhow? Capital investment, that's what!

definitions.note: capital here is the head, and an investment is something put on, clothing it

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A philistine scoffs at art and suggests that capital investment is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks financial but means head, and 'investment' means something one is vested in: a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater-style hat woven from straw is headwear, something the head is dressed in.

clue.text: Anticipate a charge for retaining metal containers

indicators.note: retaining means holding something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
ores are rocks containing metal

explanation.surface: A fee is levied for keeping tins and other metal containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal containers' looks like tins but means rocks that contain metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to see it coming before it happens, to predict it.

clue.text: Dining irregularly, a social worker gets resentful

indicators.note: irregularly means not in the usual order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: an ant is a social insect, and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: A social worker is upset about having to eat at odd hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' looks like a council employee but is the insect ANT; 'irregularly' rearranges DINING into INDIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indignant is feeling angry at unfair treatment, which is being aggrieved.

clue.text: Being sorely tried, one's leaving

indicators.note: sorely suggests something badly hurt, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone tested to the limit decides to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorely' rearranges the letters of TRIED and ONE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is the act of abandoning a post or a person, a going away.

clue.text: Intends to live on!

definitions.meaning: intends as a verb, has in mind
one's income or resources for living

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for having a purpose and the noun for the money a person survives on.

clue.text: Some of the reporters euphemistic language

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Journalists are said to use softened, polite language.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Weed turning into club to find soak

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club

indicators.note: turning says the word for weed is read the other way round

parts.note: a tare is a weed found in cornfields

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a weed coiling round a club and decides to steep it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the weed, giving ERAT, and 'into' sets that inside the club.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate is to soften something by steeping it in liquid.

clue.text: Material assistance should be rewarded

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
aid means help

explanation.surface: Help given in kind ought to be paid back.
explanation.definitionFit: Repaid means given something back in return, so recompensed.

clue.text: Hems torn net

indicators.note: torn suggests ripped apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor finds the hems on a piece of netting ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is netting, a fabric of open interlaced strands.

clue.text: The service providing regular music

parts.note: even means regular or steady
a song is a piece of music

explanation.surface: A church service supplying steady music.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer office of the Church of England, a church service.

clue.text: Put back this month in real money

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of the present month in old business letters
L stands for pound, from the Latin librae

explanation.surface: Something is restored this month, paid for in hard cash.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is an old commercial abbreviation for 'this month'; it goes into REAL followed by L for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall something is to set it up again in its former place.

clue.text: Refuse to hold pose such stupidity!

indicators.note: to hold means to keep inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to deny is to refuse
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the foolishness of declining to model for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish but is the verb DENY.
explanation.definitionFit: Density in the sense of thickness of mind is dullness, slowness of understanding.

clue.text: Hoarding hosiery?

definitions.meaning: putting by supplies, laying in a stock
a nylon or silk leg covering

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of building up supplies and a garment for the leg and foot.

clue.text: Making a big noise return a gold ring

indicators.note: return says the word a and the heraldic word for gold are read backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shouts loudly about getting a gold ring back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses A and the heraldic gold together, giving ROA; OR for gold is a heraldry convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaring describes producing a loud deep sound, like a bellowing lion.

clue.text: Too shy, so appears gloomy

parts.note: over means too, as in overly
to shy is to throw, and so is to cast

explanation.surface: A very timid person looks depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like timid but means throw, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dark and dull with cloud, so dismal.

clue.text: Tot carrying present held tightly

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to tot up is to add
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A toddler with a gift grips it firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhered means stuck fast to something, clinging firmly.

clue.text: Unwilling to drive in the end

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: end is a finish
to force is to drive or compel

explanation.surface: Someone was reluctant to take the wheel in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Enforced means compelled rather than voluntary, as in enforced idleness.

clue.text: A barrel exceptional sack

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A remarkable sack is compared to a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a wooden container for liquids such as wine or beer.

clue.text: Always in fashion for the very conventional

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Being permanently fashionable suits only the most conformist.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'the very'; 'fashion for' and 'conventional' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, forever.

clue.text: At one time quiet and open

parts.note: ex means former, at one time
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Something was once silent and unfolded.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to spread out or unfold, as a flower opens.

clue.text: A cheat in the matter of love

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
re means concerning, in the matter of

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of cheating where romance is concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to love deeply and worship.

clue.text: Posts the prize-money

definitions.meaning: pointed wooden poles driven into the ground
the sum to be won in a race or game

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both pointed posts and the money put up for a contest.

clue.text: A number inside break out for a lark

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to escape is to break out
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A group of prisoners break out just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' gives the Roman numeral D for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring adventure, a prank or frolic.

clue.text: This factory could well go to pot!

definitions.meaning: a growing thing that might be put into a flowerpot

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an industrial works and a growing thing set in soil.

clue.text: Country folk can be pert as any

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may be made into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Rural people can be as cheeky as anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The peasantry are the rural labouring class taken together.
